question.:question/problem:
If
$C = \begin{bmatrix}-2 & -3 \\ 8 & k\end{bmatrix}$
and
$det(C) = 12$, what is the value of $k$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a $2\times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

$$
\begin{vmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{vmatrix}=ad-bc.
$$

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C) & =\begin{vmatrix}-2 & -3 \\ 8 & k\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(-2)\cdot k-(-3)\cdot 8 \\  & =-2k+24\end{aligned}
$$

Since $det(C)=12$, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C) & =12 \\ -2k+24 & =12 \\ -2k & =-12 \\ k & =6\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
If
$A = \begin{bmatrix}2 + t & 2t \\ 1 & 2 - t\end{bmatrix}$
and $det(A) = 5$, what is the value of $t$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a $2\times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

$$
\begin{vmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{vmatrix}=ad-bc.
$$

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =\begin{vmatrix}2+t & 2t \\ 1 & 2-t\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(2+t)(2-t)-2t\cdot 1 \\  & =4-{t}^{2}-2t \\  & =-{t}^{2}-2t+4\end{aligned}
$$

Since $det(A)=5$, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =5 \\ -{t}^{2}-2t+4 & =5 \\ -{t}^{2}-2t-1 & =0 \\ {t}^{2}+2t+1 & =0 \\ (t+1)^{2} & =0 \\ t & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{vmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{vmatrix}=ad-bc.

question.:question/problem:

$T=\begin{bmatrix}v & -2v \\ 3 & v-4\end{bmatrix}$
and $det(T)=-1$, what is the value of $v?$

$$
\begin{vmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{vmatrix}=ad-bc.

$$

\begin{aligned}det(T) & =-1 \\ {v}^{2}+2v & =-1 \\ {v}^{2}+2v+1 & =0 \\ (v+1)^{2} & =0 \\ v & =-1\end{aligned}
